blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Inventory, viewed from the CFO's chair, is not a supply chain metric — it is a working capital strategy. Every unit sitting on a shelf is cash that has been borrowed, invested, and is currently producing nothing. Every unit not on the shelf, when a customer wants it, is a sale lost and a relationship bruised. The senior leader's job is to find the line between these two costs, and to hold the organisation on it.

At executive level, inventory decisions are made with a second lens beyond service level: cash. How many days of inventory are we carrying? What would a 5% reduction free up, and where else could that cash be used? How much of today's inventory is a rational buffer, and how much is the accumulated silt of optimisation decisions nobody reviews anymore?

These are not questions for the warehouse manager. They are board questions. The companies that answer them honestly tend to have very different balance sheets, over time, from those that treat inventory as an operational afterthought.

items.q: According to the text, how should a CFO primarily view inventory?
items.why: "Inventory, viewed from the CFO's chair… is a working capital strategy."

items.q: What does the text say every unit on the shelf represents?
options: Cash that has been borrowed and invested but is producing nothing
A purely operational cost with no financial weight
items.why: "Every unit sitting on a shelf is cash that has been borrowed, invested, and is currently producing nothing."

items.q: The phrase "the accumulated silt of optimisation decisions nobody reviews anymore" most likely refers to…
options: Stock that has piled up from old choices no one revisits
items.why: Inferência: "silt" (sedimento) sugere acúmulo esquecido — estoque residual de decisões antigas, não uma reserva racional.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Setting inventory targets is best left entirely to the warehouse manager.
Inventory levels have real consequences for the balance sheet.
There is a cost to both excess stock and stockouts.
Holding too little stock can damage customer relationships.
items.why: Inferência: o texto insiste que "these are board questions", não do gerente de armazém.

items.q: What does the final paragraph imply about companies that treat inventory as "an operational afterthought"?
options: They answer the hard cash questions more honestly
They are likely to have weaker balance sheets over time
They carry no working capital risk
They tend to have stronger balance sheets over time
items.why: Inferência: o contraste implica que quem responde honestamente tem balanços melhores; o descuidado, piores.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry apresentando a revisão de capital de giro ao conselho. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you. I'll keep this brief, because the headline number does most of the talking. On the screen you can see our inventory position for the quarter, and beside it a figure I want the board to sit with: roughly thirty per cent of what we are currently holding cannot be tied to any live service-level requirement.

Let me be precise about what that means. It is not spoilage, and it is not obsolete in the accounting sense. It is stock that was ordered against forecasts, buffers, and rules of thumb that, frankly, nobody in this room can now explain. When my team went line by line and asked why a given position existed, the honest answer, more often than not, was that it had always been there.

Now, that thirty per cent is not free. It has been borrowed, it sits on our balance sheet, and it is earning us nothing. If we released even half of it in an orderly way before year-end, the working capital freed up could be redeployed into the supplier reliability programme we deferred last spring.

I'm not asking the board to approve a fire sale. I'm asking us to agree that inventory should be reviewed as a cash decision, quarterly, at this level — and that safety stock must be justified by service, not by habit.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is the central figure Harry wants the board to focus on?
options: Around 30% of inventory tied to no live service-level requirement
The full write-off of obsolete stock
items.why: "roughly thirty per cent of what we are currently holding cannot be tied to any live service-level requirement."

items.q: How does Harry describe the origin of this excess stock?
options: It is obsolete in the accounting sense
It was deliberately reserved for a new product launch
It was ordered against forecasts and rules of thumb nobody can now explain
It was damaged or spoiled in storage
items.why: "stock that was ordered against forecasts, buffers, and rules of thumb that… nobody in this room can now explain."

items.q: Where does Harry propose the freed-up working capital could go?
options: Into the supplier reliability programme deferred last spring
items.why: "the working capital freed up could be redeployed into the supplier reliability programme we deferred last spring."

items.q: When Harry says "I'm not asking the board to approve a fire sale," he is signalling that…
options: He wants the stock liquidated instantly at any price
He opposes reducing inventory at all
He is proposing to close the warehouse
He favours an orderly, controlled release rather than a panic dump
items.why: Inferência: ele contrasta 'fire sale' (venda desesperada) com 'in an orderly way' — quer liberação controlada.

items.q: What underlying principle is Harry ultimately arguing for?
options: That the board should stop reviewing inventory
That service level no longer matters
That the warehouse manager should own inventory targets
That inventory should be judged as a cash decision, not by habit
items.why: Inferência: 'reviewed as a cash decision… safety stock must be justified by service, not by habit' resume sua tese.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "That order tied up cash we had to borrow at a punishing rate." To borrow means to…
options: take money temporarily, to be repaid
items.why: To borrow = tomar emprestado, com obrigação de devolver.

items.q: "When the supplier failed, the client relationship was left badly bruised." Here bruised means…
items.why: Bruised = ferido/machucado: a relação foi abalada, não rompida.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Executives judge inventory through a second ___: cash, not just service level."
items.why: Lens = lente: uma perspectiva/critério pelo qual se analisa a decisão.

items.q: A rational buffer is best described as…
options: cash held in a separate reserve account
stock deliberately held to cover justified variability in demand
stock kept for no defensible reason
the accounting value of obsolete goods
items.why: Rational buffer = reserva racional: estoque de segurança que se justifica pela variação real de demanda.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Treating stock as an operational ___ is exactly how excess piles up unnoticed."
items.why: Afterthought = consideração secundária: algo tratado sem prioridade, e por isso negligenciado.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de capital de giro. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the liquidation plan." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We plan to free up cash by trimming excess stock before year-end." To free up means to…
items.why: Free up = liberar (recursos) para serem usados em outro lugar.

items.q: "Procurement pushed back on the deeper stock cuts." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The last review flagged the problem but no one followed through." They…
options: failed to carry the action to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Shaving a few pallets here and there won't move the needle on working capital." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, causar diferença perceptível.
